title: Macrozona sur: Hechos violentos caen 85% desde primer estado de excepción
content: According to a study by the Multigremial de La Araucanía (MGA), violent incidents in the southern macroregion (macrozona sur) of Chile have decreased by 85% since the first constitutional state of exception (EE) was declared on October 12, 2021. Prior to the EE, an average of six violent acts were recorded per week; today, only one such incident occurs every seven days on average. The study analyzes the evolution of violent events from the Biobío Region to the Los Lagos Region. The initial declaration of the EE sparked controversy and strong opposition in Congress, but four years later, the data shows a significant decline in violence. The findings were published by El Mercurio de Santiago on October 12, 2025.

title: Multigremial de La Araucanía: Informe de violencia revela más de 66 muertes en 23 años y acusa al Gobierno de no aplicar la Ley Antiterrorista en todos los casos - Araucanía Noticias Temuco
content: The Multigremial de La Araucanía released its August 2025 violence report, noting that while attacks have declined, homicides and thwarted attempts have risen sharply. The report records 1,032 violent incidents from January 2021 to the present, averaging 4.3 attacks per month. It highlights that 81 % of this year’s attacks occur in La Araucanía, with Malleco province accounting for two‑thirds of them. The organization points out that the region has suffered more than 66 deaths over 23 years of violence, most of which remain unresolved judicially. In a press statement, Patricio Santibáñez, president of the Multigremial, said, 'El terrorismo en la Macrozona Sur ya ha cobrado más de 66 vidas, la mayoría sin resolución judicial. Esa es la herida más dolorosa: familias enteras esperando justicia que nunca llega.' He further criticized the government for failing to invoke the Anti‑Terrorism Law in most cases, arguing, 'Es incomprensible que, existiendo una ley especialmente diseñada para perseguir y desarticular a grupos terroristas y de crimen organizado, el Gobierno elija omitirla.' The report calls for Chile to adopt a firm stance, applying the law in all incidents and working toward the total dismantlement of terrorism in the Macrozona Sur.

title: Tras 28 días sin atentados en la Macrozona Sur, septiembre registra cinco hechos violentos en solo una semana - El Líbero
content: In the Macrozona Sur region of Chile, five violent incidents were reported within a single week in September 2025, marking the first such activity in 28 days since the August 23, 2025, murder of forest worker Manuel León. The incidents included multiple shootings near a private residence, followed by arson attacks on a wood storage warehouse and two vehicles. The attack was reported at approximately 4:30 a.m. via a radio call to Malleco's communications center, prompting a joint operation by the Sixth Police Station of Ercilla and public order control personnel. A female adult victim reported hearing close-range gunfire before the fire started. At the scene, authorities discovered a banner with the message: 'Freedom for Mapuche prisoners. Out with forestry companies from Mapuche territory. Out with the Yana Kona, the land is not for sale, it is defended! Amulepu Tain Weichan.' No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Carabineros secured the site and deployed a protective operation. The five incidents collectively damaged nine assets, including a skidder in Loncoche, a backhoe in Pidima, and a vehicle on Route 182. Additionally, in a separate case, Alejandro Andrés Liguen Venegas was sentenced to over 27 years in prison for the murder of PDI inspector Luis Morales Balcázar during a 2020 operation in Temucuicui. The sentence included 17 years for the completed homicide, 10 years and one day for an attempted homicide, and 300 days for receiving a stolen weapon used in the crime. The regional prosecutor of La Araucanía, Roberto Garrido, noted that between October 2020 and May 2021, three police officer homicides occurred in the region—two Carabineros (Eugenio Nain and Francisco Benavides) and one PDI officer (Morales Balcázar)—and emphasized that evidence gathered in these cases enabled the prosecution of suspects, with the goal of dismantling armed criminal organizations operating in the area.

title: Más de mil días bajo estado de excepción en la Macrozona Sur: informe revela que violencia se redujo en 37% y ataques a infraestructura en 47% - La Tercera
content: According to a report by the Observatorio sobre Crimen Organizado y Terrorismo (OCRIT) of the Universidad Andrés Bello, the state of emergency in the Macrozona Sur region of Chile has been in place for over 1,082 days, making it the longest state of emergency since the return to democracy. The report, presented by Pablo Urquízar, shows that the state of emergency has reduced violence by 37% and attacks on infrastructure by 47%. However, the report also highlights that the state of emergency has had a heterogeneous effect on the region, with some areas experiencing a significant reduction in violence while others have seen an increase. Urquízar emphasized the need for a territorial approach to address the root causes of the violence and to prioritize resources and operations in the most affected areas. He also highlighted the importance of protecting human rights and the security of the population, citing a 58% reduction in fatalities and a 50% reduction in injuries. The report also notes that the introduction of transnational organized crime could exacerbate the situation, posing a strategic risk to the region. Urquízar identified five key challenges that need to be addressed, including the need for a comprehensive vision of the problem, avoiding the normalization of the exception, and strengthening intelligence gathering.

title: Homicidios en Chile: las horas y los días donde más se comenten asesinatos en el país
content: The Centro para la Prevención de Homicidios y Delitos Violentos (CPHDV) of the Fiscalía Nacional released a report on homicide victims in Chile for the first half of 2025. The data show that 33.1% of the 511 victims occurred on weekends, with 17.4% (89 cases) on Saturdays and 15.7% (80 cases) on Sundays, indicating a concentration of violence at the end of the week. By time of day, the 18:00‑23:59 window accounted for 31.9% (163 victims) and the 00:00‑05:59 window for 29.2% (149 victims), together representing 61.1% of all cases. The most frequent location was the public road (55.4%), followed by private homes (27.2%), both slightly lower than the same periods in 2024. The homicide rate fell to 2.5 per 100 000 inhabitants, a 13.8% decrease from the 2.9 rate in 2024, and 74 fewer victims in absolute terms. The report cautions that "interpret variations in small sub‑categories with care, due to the effect of small numbers, and prefer annual series for structural comparisons."

title: Las Fiestas Patrias en Chile dejaron 45 muertos
content: Chile's National Holidays (Fiestas Patrias) from September 15 to 21, 2025, resulted in 45 deaths, a 40% drop from the 2024 figure, according to the Ministry of Security. Of those, 22 were homicides, down from 37 last year, as stated by interim Security Minister Rafael Collado: 'Este año tenemos 40% menos de homicidios respecto de las Fiestas Patrias del año pasado. Ese número se contabiliza desde el 15 hasta el 21 de septiembre. En términos numérico, pasamos de 37 a 22 víctimas'. Only one homicide stemmed from a fight in a 'fonda' in Puchuncaví. Car accidents accounted for 23 fatalities, with 563 incidents recorded, 70% in urban areas and 29% rural, according to General Víctor Vielma, head of Traffic, Roads and Road Safety: 'lamentablemente fallecieron 23 personas este año 2025 y las causas asociadas a estos siniestros con consecuencias fatales fue por la conducción a exceso de velocidad, la conducción no atenta y principalmente una causa que viene sostenida y en aumento, que es la exposición del peatón a riesgo de atropello con consecuencias fatales'. Transport Minister Juan Carlos Muñoz highlighted the death of an 11‑year‑old girl in Pucón: 'De estas 23 personas, tenemos una persona que es una niña y que acentúa esta situación que pasa en Chile, de que perdemos un niño a la semana producto de siniestros viales'. A government official added: 'Desde el viernes 17 hasta el domingo 21 perdimos un promedio de cinco personas cada día. El año pasado perdimos siete en ese período, lo que habla de que este año, en ese sentido, fue mejor que el año pasado. Pero uno no se puede felicitar, uno no se puede alegrar cuando estamos presentando este tipo de estadística'.

title: Primer semestre de 2025 tuvo 511 víctimas de homicidio consumado: RM, Valparaíso y Biobío concentraron crímenes
content: The National Victim Report on Homicides in Chile for the first half of 2025, presented by the Minister of Public Security Luis Cordero, the national prosecutor Ángel Valencia, the Deputy Secretary of Crime Prevention Carolina Leitao, and police officials, shows a total of 551 homicide victims, a 2.5 per 100 000‑person rate. This is a drop of 74 victims and a 13.8 % reduction in the rate compared with 581 victims (2.9 per 100 000) recorded in the same period of 2024. The Metropolitan region led with 238 victims, followed by Valparaíso (55) and Biobío (40). 45.8 % of homicides were committed with firearms and 37.6 % with sharp objects. Men accounted for 88.6 % of victims, women 11.2 %; 54.8 % of victims were aged 18‑39. Foreign‑national victims fell from 20.2 % in 2024 to 11.9 % in 2025. Children under 18 made up 22 victims (down from 37 in 2024). 31.8 % of deaths occurred in contexts linked to organized crime or criminal activity, 50 % in interpersonal contexts. 39.1 % of victims were in interpersonal situations, higher than 36.8 % in 2024. 17.4 % of homicides happened on Saturdays and 15.7 % on Sundays, totaling 33.1 % over the weekend; 31.9 % occurred between 18:00 and 23:59. The report also notes 24 femicide victims (one more than 2024) and 17 homicide victims in penitentiary facilities (six fewer than 2024). The report includes the quote: 'representa una disminución de 74 víctimas y una reducción de 13,8% en la tasa respecto del mismo período de 2024'. It also cites: 'lo que muestra la relevancia de considerar proporcionalmente el tamaño poblacional de cada territorio', 'El 17,4% de los homicidios ocurrieron los sábados y el 15,7% los domingos, sumando un total del 33,1% de las muertes esos dos días', 'representó el 39,1% del total de víctimas, cifra superior al 36,8% observado el primer semestre del 2024', and 'incorporan datos de víctimas de homicidios consumados en recintos penitenciarios, registrándose 17 víctimas durante el primer semestre del año 2025 (seis menos que el primer semestre del año 2024)'.

title: Atentados en el sur han caído 85% en cuatro años de estado de excepción
content: A report by the Multigremial de La Araucanía reveals an 85% decrease in violent incidents in the Macrozona Sur since the implementation of the first constitutional state of exception, decreed on October 12, 2021, by former President Sebastián Piñera. Prior to this measure, the region recorded over six attacks per week; currently, the average is one violent incident every seven days. Although President Gabriel Boric did not renew the state of exception after taking office in March 2022, it was reinstated in a limited form in May 2022 and remains in effect today in La Araucanía, and the provinces of Biobío and Arauco. Despite the positive trend, Multigremial president Patricio Santibáñez warned that terrorism remains present and called for more offensive actions, not just deterrent measures, to dismantle these groups. He emphasized that fear continues to impact both public safety and regional economic activity. Diputado Andrés Jouannet of Amarillos por Chile stated that the decline in violence is not a reason for celebration, calling it a 'shame' to rely on military presence while terrorists remain. He criticized the government for failing to take full responsibility. Similarly, former RN deputy Miguel Mellado demanded greater authority for the armed forces, arguing that the lack of political backing prevents them from engaging terrorists effectively. The Chilean Congress is set to debate a new renewal of the state of exception on Tuesday.

title: Informe de homicidios 2024: bajan los delitos, pero aumentan las víctimas e imputados menores de edad
content: The Chilean Public Ministry released its 2024 homicide report on August 29 2025, showing a 3 % drop in total cases to 3,578, but a 2 % rise in completed homicides to 1,207 (28 % of all homicides). The national victim rate fell to 6 per 100,000, a 4 % decline from 2023. However, victims and accused minors increased: 76 minor victims (6.3 % of all homicides), 68 % of those minors were 14‑17 years old, and 8.8 per 100,000 adolescents were accused. Provisional detention rose to 84 % from 69 % in 2023. Foreigners now account for 20.4 % of accused, double the 10 % in 2021, and 10 % of victims, up 10 % from the previous year. Organized‑crime homicides remain 16.5 % of total, and prison‑related homicides are more than 13 times the national rate. The report notes a reduction in unidentified accused from 42 % in 2022 to 34 % in 2024. Femicides increased from 43 to 44 cases, with a shift toward public spaces. The Ministry’s report states, 'los delitos de homicidios disminuyeron en un 2,7%; las víctimas, en un 11,2% y los imputados en un 4,1%'. It also notes, 'la participación de adolescentes imputados por homicidio se incrementó, alcanzando una tasa del 8,8 por cada 100 000 adolescentes'.

title: Homicidios consumados: 11 regiones bajan y casi 40% están ligados a crimen organizado
content: The El Mercurio de Santiago report for the first half of 2024 shows that homicide rates fell in 11 Chilean regions—Tarapacá, Antofagasta, Atacama, Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Metropolitana, O'Higgins, Ñuble, Biobío, Los Ríos, and Aysén—while five regions recorded increases: Arica y Parinacota (from 5.0 to 5.7 per 100,000), Maule (1.5 to 1.9), La Araucanía (1.9 to 2.0), Los Lagos (2.1 to 2.2), and Magallanes (1.1 to 1.6). The report notes that 'se deben observar con atención, a fin de evaluar si responden a situaciones puntuales o a transformaciones estructurales en los patrones de violencia'.
